subject: physics
title: Operational amplifiers
key_idea: An ideal operational amplifier has infinite open-loop gain and infinite input resistance. With negative feedback it becomes an amplifier whose gain is set by two resistors. Used with no feedback, it is a comparator.

blocks.text: An operational amplifier (op-amp) is a system building block with two inputs and one output. It needs a power supply as well as the signal connections.

items: The **inverting input** is marked V₋ and the **non-inverting input** is marked V₊.
It has a positive and a negative power supply connection, and the output voltage can never go beyond them.
The signal connections are the two inputs and the output.

blocks.label: Open-loop transfer function
where: V₊, V₋ = voltages at the two inputs (V)

items: An ideal op-amp has **infinite open-loop gain**.
An ideal op-amp has **infinite input resistance**, so no current enters either input.
A real op-amp has a very large but finite gain, so the output saturates at about the supply voltages.
With no feedback the gain is huge, so a tiny difference between the inputs drives the output to saturation.
If V₊ is greater than V₋, the output goes to the positive supply voltage.
If V₊ is less than V₋, the output goes to the negative supply voltage.
The circuit compares an input voltage with a reference voltage.
Vₒᵤₜ = A_OL (V₊ − V₋), and the output cannot exceed the supply voltages.
An ideal op-amp has infinite gain and infinite input resistance.
With no feedback it works as a comparator.

blocks.text: Negative feedback joins the output back to the inverting input through a feedback resistor R_f. The gain then depends only on the resistors.

items.meaning: In the inverting amplifier the non-inverting input is at 0 V, and feedback holds the inverting input at almost 0 V too.

items.text: V₊ is at 0 V and the gain is huge, so V₋ is also almost 0 V.
No current enters the op-amp, so all the current through Rᵢₙ passes through R_f.
The current is I = Vᵢₙ ÷ Rᵢₙ, because the voltage across Rᵢₙ is Vᵢₙ − 0.
The voltage across R_f is 0 − Vₒᵤₜ, so Vₒᵤₜ = −I R_f.
Substituting I gives the gain equation.

blocks.text: The minus sign means the output is the inverse of the input: it is in antiphase.

blocks.label: Non-inverting amplifier gain
where: R₁ = resistor from the inverting input to 0 V (Ω)

items: The input goes to V₊, and the output is in phase with the input.
The gain is always at least 1.
Derivation is not required.

diagram.alt: A practice question. Calculate the output voltage of an inverting amplifier from the two resistances and the input voltage.
diagram.question: An inverting amplifier has Rᵢₙ = {Rin} kΩ and R_f = {Rf} kΩ. The input voltage is {Vin} V. Calculate the output voltage.

items: Inverting gain = −R_f ÷ Rᵢₙ, found using a virtual earth at the inverting input.
Non-inverting gain = 1 + R_f ÷ R₁.

blocks.text: The inverting amplifier can add several inputs. A different arrangement subtracts two inputs. Neither derivation is required.

blocks.label: Summing amplifier
blocks.formula: Vₒᵤₜ = −R_f (V₁ ÷ R₁ + V₂ ÷ R₂ + V₃ ÷ R₃ + …)
where: R₁, R₂, R₃ = their input resistors (Ω)

blocks.label: Difference amplifier
where: V₊, V₋ = the two input voltages (V)
R_f ÷ R₁ = gain set by the resistors

items: A summing amplifier gives the inverted, weighted sum of its inputs.
A difference amplifier amplifies the difference between its two inputs.

blocks.text: A real op-amp falls short of the ideal in several ways.

items: The open-loop gain is large but finite, and it falls as the signal frequency rises.
The input resistance is high but finite.
The output cannot go beyond the supply voltages, so a large output is clipped.
The **frequency response curve** plots gain against frequency. The gain is flat at low frequency and then falls.
The constant is fixed for a given device.
A higher gain from the feedback resistors therefore means a smaller bandwidth.
Real op-amps have finite gain and input resistance, and gain falls at high frequency.
Gain × bandwidth is constant for a given device.

checks.q: An op-amp is used as a comparator. State the output when V₊ is greater than V₋.
checks.a: The output saturates at the positive supply voltage.

checks.q: An inverting amplifier has Rᵢₙ = 2.0 kΩ and R_f = 20 kΩ. Calculate the output for an input of 0.30 V.
A device has a gain-bandwidth product of 1.0 × 10⁶ Hz. Calculate the bandwidth when the closed-loop gain is 50.
